title: Finite matrix coordinates for a bounded projective complex over a DVR
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $a\leq b$ be integers and let $P^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules: its differentials $d^i:P^i\to P^{i+1}$ are $R$-linear and satisfy $d^{i+1}d^i=0$. Suppose $P^i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$ and each $P^i$ is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Then there exist integers $n_i\geq0$, with $n_i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$, $R$-linear isomorphisms $e_i:R^{n_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}P^i$, and matrices $D_i\in\operatorname{Mat}_{n_{i+1}\times n_i}(R)$ [def-weil-matrix] such that
$$d^i e_i=e_{i+1}D_i,\qquad D_{i+1}D_i=0.$$
Here a matrix acts on coordinate column vectors, and rank-zero modules and rectangular matrices are allowed. Thus $M^i=R^{n_i}$ with differential $D_i$ is a bounded finite free scalar complex supported in the same interval, and the $e_i$ form an isomorphism of complexes $M^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}P^\bullet$. No change of scalar ring or replacement by a merely quasi-isomorphic unbounded complex is required.

source.place: Clause (1), finite projective to finite free scalar basis replacement; algebra.tex lemma-characterize-projective (Stacks Tag 05CF) and more-algebra.tex lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat (Stacks Tag 0AUW), part (3), followed by explicit coordinate transport.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], for each $i$ choose split maps $j:P^i\to F$ and $s:F\to P^i$ with $sj=1$ and $F=\bigoplus_I R$ free. If $0\ne r\in R$ and $rx=0$, then $rj(x)=0$. The domain condition in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] forces every coordinate of $j(x)$ to vanish, so $x=sj(x)=0$. Thus every $P^i$ is torsion-free.

source.place: Tag 05CF, lemma-characterize-projective, (1) implies (2); coordinatewise torsion-freeness over a domain

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] to $P^i$: the ring is the given DVR, finite generation is assumed, and step 1 gives torsion-freeness. Choose a finite basis, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and enumerate it to obtain $e_i:R^{n_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}P^i$ for each $i\in[a,b]$. Outside this finite interval take $n_i=0$ and the unique linear isomorphism $R^0\cong P^i=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat, part (3), applied to the DVR; finite basis choices

proof.text: Let $u_j$ be the standard coordinate vectors of $R^{n_i}$. Define the matrix [def-weil-matrix] by $D_i(k,j)=(e_{i+1}^{-1}d^i e_i(u_j))_k$. For $v=\sum_jv_j u_j$, linearity gives $e_{i+1}^{-1}d^i e_i(v)=\sum_jv_j(e_{i+1}^{-1}d^i e_i(u_j))=D_i v$. Hence $d^i e_i=e_{i+1}D_i$. Empty index sets give the same equality because the sums are zero.

source.place: Clause (1), explicit column-coordinate formula for differentials on the finite free scalar models

proof.text: For every coordinate vector $v\in R^{n_i}$, step 3 gives $e_{i+2}(D_{i+1}D_i v)=d^{i+1}e_{i+1}(D_i v)=d^{i+1}d^i e_i(v)=0$. Injectivity of $e_{i+2}$ shows $D_{i+1}D_i v=0$. Apply this to each standard vector $u_j$: its $k$-th coordinate is the $(k,j)$ entry of the matrix product, so every entry of $D_{i+1}D_i$ is zero, including empty rectangular cases.

source.place: Clause (1), square-zero relation after the explicit change of coordinates

proof.text: Put $M^i=R^{n_i}$ and $d_M^i(v)=D_i v$. Step 4 makes this a cochain complex. Step 3 is exactly the chain-map equation for $(e_i):M^\bullet\to P^\bullet$. Multiplying that equation by the inverse isomorphisms gives $D_i e_i^{-1}=e_{i+1}^{-1}d^i$, so $(e_i^{-1})$ is an inverse chain map; both composites are the identity in every degree. The chosen $n_i=0$ outside $[a,b]$ gives both support bounds, with finite free terms over the original ring $R$.

source.place: Clause (1), strict complex isomorphism and unchanged finite support interval

Edge cases tested: P=0, a=b, the two-term complex R--π^m-->R, R/π excluded as non-projective, and a non-complete DVR.
